questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The earth ___ round the sun.
questions.explanation: A scientific fact takes the simple present, with -s for a singular subject.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: At 8 p.m. yesterday, we ___ dinner.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a stated past time takes the past continuous.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ in Mysuru for three years before she moved to Kolkata.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past events takes the past perfect: had lived.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: I ___ my keys; can you help me look for them?
questions.explanation: A past action with a present result is expressed by the present perfect.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: He ___ to the gym every day, but today he is resting.
questions.explanation: A daily habit takes the simple present.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: I am working here since March.
We have known each other for years.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb used in the present perfect with 'for'; the other sentences misuse tense.

questions.q: Change into the simple future tense: 'They visited the museum.'
questions.explanation: The simple future is formed with will and the base form.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'I have met him yesterday.'
questions.explanation: The present perfect cannot be used with a finished time expression.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The students ___ in the library.
questions.explanation: 'Students' is plural, so the verb is 'are'.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: She ___ a beautiful voice.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes 'has'.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The teacher, together with the students, ___ gone on a trip.
questions.explanation: 'Together with' does not make the subject plural; the verb agrees with 'teacher'.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Half of the cake ___ eaten.
questions.explanation: 'Cake' is singular, so the verb is singular.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Measles ___ a contagious disease.
questions.explanation: 'Measles' ends in -s but is a singular name of a disease.

questions.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Each of the boys have a bat.
A number of reasons was given.
Every boy and every girl was given a certificate.
questions.explanation: Subjects joined by 'and' but each preceded by 'every' are treated as singular.

questions.q: Correct the error: 'My trousers is too long.'
questions.explanation: Trousers, like scissors, is always plural in grammar.

questions.q: Rewrite correctly: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers was present.'
questions.answer: Neither the principal nor the teachers were present.
keyPoints: with neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the subject closer to it.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: He is ___ MLA.
questions.explanation: 'MLA' is pronounced 'em-el-ay', which begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: She wore ___ red saree.
questions.explanation: 'Red' begins with a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct article: He plays ___ guitar very well.
questions.explanation: 'The' is used with musical instruments after 'play'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ of my friends lives in Delhi.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun and a singular verb, which matches 'lives'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: How ___ rice do you need for the recipe?
questions.explanation: 'Rice' is uncountable, so 'much' is used.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: He has a one-year-old son and an one-rupee coin.
She visited an orphanage on Sunday.
questions.explanation: 'Orphanage' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is correct; the other sentences use the wrong article.

questions.q: Fill in with a, an or the: 'She asked for ___ apple and ___ orange. ___ apple was sweet.'
keyPoints: the for the apple already mentioned
questions.explanation: The first mentions are indefinite; the second mention of the apple is definite.

questions.q: Explain why 'school' has no article in 'He went to school' but has one in 'He went to the school to meet the principal'.
questions.answer: Without 'the', school refers to the purpose of the place, studying. With 'the', it refers to a particular school building he visited for another reason.
keyPoints: no article: the institution and its purpose
questions.explanation: The article shows whether we speak of an activity or a specific place.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: He was born ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: 'On' is used with days of the week.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: The shop opens ___ nine o'clock.
questions.explanation: 'At' is used with clock times.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: She is proud ___ her son.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'proud' is followed by 'of'.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: He is suffering ___ fever.
questions.explanation: The verb 'suffer' takes 'from' with an illness.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: Work hard, ___ you will fail.
questions.explanation: 'Or' means 'otherwise' and joins a command to the result of not following it.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: He congratulated me for my success.
He congratulated me on my success.
He congratulated me at my success.
He congratulated me with my success.
questions.explanation: 'Congratulate' is followed by 'on'.

questions.q: Join using 'as soon as': 'He saw the snake. He ran away.'
questions.answer: As soon as he saw the snake, he ran away.
keyPoints: as soon as shows immediate sequence
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' joins two actions that follow each other immediately.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks with prepositions: 'She is good ___ music and keen ___ learning the sitar.'
questions.explanation: These adjectives take fixed prepositions.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ not swim, so I stayed on the shore.
questions.explanation: 'Could not' expresses inability in the past.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ you please open the window?
questions.explanation: 'Could you please...?' is a polite request.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: Take your raincoat; it ___ rain this afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses a possibility.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: ___ we go for a walk after dinner?
questions.explanation: 'Shall we...?' is used to make a suggestion.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: Visitors ___ not feed the animals.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition.

questions.q: Which sentence gives advice?
questions.explanation: 'Should' is used for advice.

questions.q: Rewrite using 'should': 'It is advisable to save some money every month.'
questions.answer: You should save some money every month.
keyPoints: base form of the verb follows
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice or says what is a good idea.

questions.q: Explain the difference in meaning between 'He should have come' and 'He must have come'.
questions.answer: 'He should have come' means it was his duty to come, but he did not. 'He must have come' means I conclude that he came.
keyPoints: must have = logical conclusion about the past
questions.explanation: Modal + have + past participle can express regret or deduction.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: The door ___ by the watchman.
questions.explanation: The door receives the action, so the passive 'was opened' is used.

questions.q: Choose the correct verb: Rice ___ in many parts of India.
questions.explanation: A general fact in the passive: is grown.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'She was singing a song.'
options: A song was sung by her.
A song was being sung by her.
A song is being sung by her.
A song had been sung by her.
questions.explanation: Past continuous active becomes was/were being + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'They will build a dam.'
options: A dam is built by them.
A dam would be built by them.
A dam will built by them.
A dam will be built by them.
questions.explanation: Simple future passive: will be + past participle.

questions.q: Choose the passive voice of: 'The boy has eaten the apple.'
options: The apple has been eaten by the boy.
The apple was eaten by the boy.
The apple is eaten by the boy.
The apple had been eaten by the boy.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes has/have been + past participle.

questions.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The tap was fixed by Rahul.
questions.explanation: In the passive the subject (tap) receives the action.

questions.q: Change into the passive voice: 'The children sang the national anthem.'
questions.answer: The national anthem was sung by the children.
questions.explanation: Simple past passive: was + past participle.

questions.q: Change into the active voice: 'The prizes will be distributed by the Chief Guest.'
questions.answer: The Chief Guest will distribute the prizes.
keyPoints: will be distributed becomes will distribute
questions.explanation: Remove 'be + past participle' and use the base verb after will.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I play football.'
options: He said that he played football.
He said that I played football.
He said that he will play football.
He said that he had play football.
questions.explanation: The simple present becomes the simple past and 'I' becomes 'he'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: They said, 'We are winning.'
options: They said that we were winning.
They said that they would be winning.
They said that they were winning.
They said that they have been winning.
questions.explanation: 'We' becomes 'they' and the present continuous becomes the past continuous.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I saw him yesterday.'
options: She said that she had seen him tomorrow.
She said that I had seen him the day before.
She said that she has seen him the day before.
She said that she had seen him the day before.
questions.explanation: Simple past becomes past perfect and 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: He asked, 'Can you swim?'
options: He asked me that I could swim.
He asked me if I could swim.
He asked me could I swim.
He asked me what I could swim.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if', and 'can' becomes 'could'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: The teacher said to the student, 'Work hard.'
options: The teacher said the student work hard.
The teacher advised the student that work hard.
The teacher advised the student to work hard.
The teacher asked the student if he worked hard.
questions.explanation: A command or advice is reported with 'advised ... to + verb'.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: Mother said to me, 'May God bless you!'
options: Mother prayed that God might bless me.
Mother said that God may bless me.
Mother asked God to bless her.
Mother prayed that God bless me.
questions.explanation: A blessing or wish is reported with 'prayed that' and 'might'.

questions.q: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, 'Where are you going?'
questions.answer: He asked me where I was going.
questions.explanation: A wh-question is reported with the same question word.

questions.q: Change into direct speech: The mother told her son not to play near the road.
questions.answer: The mother said to her son, 'Do not play near the road.'
questions.explanation: A reported negative command becomes a direct 'Do not...' sentence.

questions.q: The part of a sentence that says something about the subject is called the
questions.explanation: The predicate tells what the subject does or is.

questions.q: Combine using 'both ... and': 'He is honest. He is hardworking.'
options: He is both honest or hardworking.
Both he is honest and hardworking.
He both is honest and hardworking.
He is both honest and hardworking.
questions.explanation: 'Both' and 'and' must come directly before the two words joined.

questions.q: Rewrite using 'unless': 'If you do not work hard, you will fail.'
options: Unless you do not work hard, you will fail.
Unless you worked hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will not fail.
Unless you work hard, you will fail.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not', so the verb after it is positive.

questions.q: Change into a simple sentence: 'He went to the market so that he might buy fruit.'
options: He went to the market for buy fruit.
He went to the market to buy fruit.
He went to the market for to buy fruit.
He went to the market and buy fruit.
questions.explanation: A clause of purpose can be shortened to 'to + verb'.

questions.q: Change into the superlative degree: 'Gold is more precious than any other metal.'
options: Gold is the more precious metal.
Gold is the most precious metal.
Gold is the precious metal most.
questions.explanation: The superlative uses 'the most + adjective'.

questions.q: In 'He stayed at home because he was ill', the clause 'because he was ill' is a/an
questions.explanation: It tells why he stayed at home, so it is an adverb clause of reason.

questions.q: Change into an exclamatory sentence: 'The sky is very blue.'
questions.explanation: 'How + adjective' forms an exclamation.

questions.q: Combine using 'not only ... but also': 'She sings well. She dances well.'
questions.answer: She not only sings well but also dances well.
keyPoints: not only before the first verb phrase
questions.explanation: The pair joins two parallel parts of the sentence.

questions.q: Which punctuation mark is used to show possession?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe shows that something belongs to someone.

questions.q: Which words need capital letters in: 'on monday we visited the red fort.'?
questions.explanation: The first word of the sentence and the names of a day and a monument begin with capitals.

questions.q: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory word 'Yes'.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: A comma follows each part of the split quotation before and after the speaker tag.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the colon correctly?
options: The shop sells three things: books, pens and bags.
The shop sells three things; books, pens and bags.
The shop sells; three things, books pens and bags.
The shop sells three things, books: pens and bags.
questions.explanation: A colon after a complete statement introduces a list.

questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: Its a lovely day, isn't it
It's a lovely day isn't it?
It's a lovely day, isn't it?
Its a lovely day, isnt it?
questions.explanation: It's has an apostrophe, a comma sets off the tag question, and the sentence ends with a question mark.

questions.q: Punctuate correctly: rohan said i am going to delhi on friday
questions.answer: Rohan said, 'I am going to Delhi on Friday.'
keyPoints: capital letters for names and days
questions.explanation: Direct speech is placed in inverted commas after a comma.

questions.q: Why does 'the girls' room' take an apostrophe but 'the girls play' does not?
questions.answer: In 'the girls' room' the apostrophe shows possession (the room belongs to the girls). In 'the girls play' the -s only makes 'girl' plural, so no apostrophe is needed.
questions.explanation: Plurals and possessives are different things.

questions.q: Choose the synonym of 'courage'.
questions.explanation: Courage and bravery have the same meaning.

questions.q: Choose the antonym of 'victory'.
questions.explanation: 'Defeat' is the opposite of 'victory'.

questions.q: A person who has just started learning something is called a
questions.explanation: A novice is a beginner.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The rule is 'i before e except after c', so receive.

questions.q: The prefix 'un-' in 'unhappy' means
questions.explanation: 'Un-' gives the opposite meaning: not happy.

questions.q: Something that is 'ephemeral' is
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means short-lived.

questions.q: Form verbs from the words 'beauty', 'strength' and 'class'.
questions.explanation: Suffixes such as -ify and -en turn nouns into verbs.

questions.q: Explain the difference between 'complement' and 'compliment', with a sentence for each.
questions.answer: 'Complement' means something that completes or goes well with another: The scarf complements her dress. 'Compliment' means an expression of praise: He paid her a compliment.
questions.explanation: The words sound alike but have different meanings.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to face the music' mean?
options: to accept the consequences of one's actions
questions.explanation: It means to accept the unpleasant results of what one has done.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'a drop in the ocean' mean?
options: a very small amount compared with what is needed
questions.explanation: It describes something too small to make much difference.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'to hit the sack' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Hit the sack' is an informal way of saying to go to bed.

questions.q: What does the idiom 'out of the blue' mean?
questions.explanation: It means suddenly and without warning.

questions.q: What does the phrasal verb 'put up with' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Put up with' means to tolerate something unpleasant.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: The teacher told us to ___ our books and begin the test.
questions.explanation: 'Put away' means to store something in its place.

questions.q: Explain the idiom 'to sit on the fence' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: It means to avoid taking sides in a dispute: Meena sat on the fence during the debate and supported neither team.
keyPoints: means refusing to choose a side
questions.explanation: The idiom pictures someone perched between two sides.

questions.q: Explain the phrasal verb 'take after' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: 'Take after' means to resemble an older family member: She takes after her mother in her love of music.
keyPoints: means to resemble a parent or relative
questions.explanation: It is used for family likeness in looks or character.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Every year, the students of Class 10 plant saplings in the school ground. Mr. Sinha, the science teacher, gives each pair a sapling and a small board with their names. Throughout the year, the pairs water and protect their plants. By the next planting day, most of the saplings from the previous year are standing strong and green.' Who gives each pair a sapling?
questions.explanation: Mr. Sinha, the science teacher, gives them out.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Every year, the students of Class 10 plant saplings in the school ground. Mr. Sinha, the science teacher, gives each pair a sapling and a small board with their names. Throughout the year, the pairs water and protect their plants. By the next planting day, most of the saplings from the previous year are standing strong and green.' What is written on the small board?
questions.explanation: The board carries the pair's names.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Every year, the students of Class 10 plant saplings in the school ground. Mr. Sinha, the science teacher, gives each pair a sapling and a small board with their names. Throughout the year, the pairs water and protect their plants. By the next planting day, most of the saplings from the previous year are standing strong and green.' What is the likely purpose of this activity?
options: To teach students responsibility for living things
To earn money for the school
questions.explanation: Pairs care for their saplings all year, which builds responsibility.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Every year, the students of Class 10 plant saplings in the school ground. Mr. Sinha, the science teacher, gives each pair a sapling and a small board with their names. Throughout the year, the pairs water and protect their plants. By the next planting day, most of the saplings from the previous year are standing strong and green.' How do the students look after their saplings?
questions.answer: The pairs water their saplings and protect them throughout the year.
keyPoints: they protect them through the year
questions.explanation: The third sentence says this.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Indian peacock, India's national bird, is known for its long, colourful tail feathers. During the rainy season, the male spreads these feathers into a large fan and dances to attract the female. Contrary to what many people think, the long feathers are not the true tail but a train of feathers that grow above it.' Which bird is India's national bird?
questions.explanation: The first sentence names the Indian peacock.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Indian peacock, India's national bird, is known for its long, colourful tail feathers. During the rainy season, the male spreads these feathers into a large fan and dances to attract the female. Contrary to what many people think, the long feathers are not the true tail but a train of feathers that grow above it.' Why does the male peacock spread its feathers?
questions.explanation: The passage says he dances to attract the female.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Indian peacock, India's national bird, is known for its long, colourful tail feathers. During the rainy season, the male spreads these feathers into a large fan and dances to attract the female. Contrary to what many people think, the long feathers are not the true tail but a train of feathers that grow above it.' What surprising fact does the passage give about the long feathers?
options: They are not the true tail but a train above it
They fall off in the rains
questions.explanation: The last sentence corrects a common belief.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'The Indian peacock, India's national bird, is known for its long, colourful tail feathers. During the rainy season, the male spreads these feathers into a large fan and dances to attract the female. Contrary to what many people think, the long feathers are not the true tail but a train of feathers that grow above it.' When and why does the male peacock dance?
questions.answer: He dances in the rainy season to attract the female.
questions.explanation: The second sentence gives both.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'On the day of the school sports meet, Dev woke up with a sore ankle. He wanted to run the relay, but his coach told him to rest. Dev was upset, yet he stayed at the track and cheered for his teammates with all his strength. When his team won, the captain handed him the baton to hold up with the trophy. "You ran this race with your voice," she said.' What was wrong with Dev on the day of the meet?
questions.explanation: He woke up with a sore ankle.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'On the day of the school sports meet, Dev woke up with a sore ankle. He wanted to run the relay, but his coach told him to rest. Dev was upset, yet he stayed at the track and cheered for his teammates with all his strength. When his team won, the captain handed him the baton to hold up with the trophy. "You ran this race with your voice," she said.' What did Dev do after the coach told him to rest?
options: He stayed and cheered for his teammates
questions.explanation: He stayed at the track and cheered with all his strength.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'On the day of the school sports meet, Dev woke up with a sore ankle. He wanted to run the relay, but his coach told him to rest. Dev was upset, yet he stayed at the track and cheered for his teammates with all his strength. When his team won, the captain handed him the baton to hold up with the trophy. "You ran this race with your voice," she said.' What did the captain mean by 'You ran this race with your voice'?
options: Dev's cheering helped the team to win
questions.explanation: She is saying that his encouragement counted as his contribution to the win.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'On the day of the school sports meet, Dev woke up with a sore ankle. He wanted to run the relay, but his coach told him to rest. Dev was upset, yet he stayed at the track and cheered for his teammates with all his strength. When his team won, the captain handed him the baton to hold up with the trophy. "You ran this race with your voice," she said.' Was Dev's behaviour sporting? Give a reason from the passage.
questions.answer: Yes. Although he was upset at missing the relay, he stayed at the track and cheered for his teammates with all his strength.
keyPoints: he was upset but did not sulk
he stayed and cheered for the team
questions.explanation: He put the team's success above his own disappointment.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Zero is one of the most important ideas in mathematics. It acts as a placeholder, which lets us tell the difference between 10, 100 and 1000. Ancient Indian mathematicians treated zero as a number in its own right and developed rules for using it. Today it is used everywhere, from the decimal number system to computers.' How does the first sentence describe zero?
options: One of the most important ideas in mathematics
questions.explanation: The first sentence calls it one of the most important ideas in mathematics.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Zero is one of the most important ideas in mathematics. It acts as a placeholder, which lets us tell the difference between 10, 100 and 1000. Ancient Indian mathematicians treated zero as a number in its own right and developed rules for using it. Today it is used everywhere, from the decimal number system to computers.' Which numbers does the passage say zero helps us tell apart?
questions.explanation: The second sentence names 10, 100 and 1000.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Zero is one of the most important ideas in mathematics. It acts as a placeholder, which lets us tell the difference between 10, 100 and 1000. Ancient Indian mathematicians treated zero as a number in its own right and developed rules for using it. Today it is used everywhere, from the decimal number system to computers.' What does 'placeholder' mean as used in the passage?
options: A symbol that has no meaning
A symbol that holds a position so that the value of the other digits is clear
The last digit of a number
questions.explanation: Zero fills a position, which separates 10 from 100 and 1000.

questions.q: Read the passage. 'Zero is one of the most important ideas in mathematics. It acts as a placeholder, which lets us tell the difference between 10, 100 and 1000. Ancient Indian mathematicians treated zero as a number in its own right and developed rules for using it. Today it is used everywhere, from the decimal number system to computers.' What did ancient Indian mathematicians do with zero?
questions.answer: They treated zero as a number in its own right and developed rules for using it.
questions.explanation: The third sentence states this.
